title: POC scoping - Acme Healthcare x Redwood
next_steps: Redwood to share POC runbook and access checklist by 2025-02-14
Customer to provision test VPC peering and provide bastion credentials by 2025-02-20
Schedule kickoff and infra access session week of 2025-02-17
action_items: Sam Chen | Send POC playbook + pricing lanes | 2025-02-14
Priya Patel | Draft benchmark plan (QPS, token mix, latency SLOs) | 2025-02-14
Elaine Park | Create service account + SSO test user, share with Redwood | 2025-02-20
Marcus Reyes | Provide sample workload traces and 1 week of traffic logs | 2025-02-15
summary: POC scoping call to align on success criteria, workload sizing and milestones for a 4-week Redwood POC. Discussed access (VPC, KMS), benchmarks (QPS, token distribution, latency SLO), and timeline: kickoff, infra access, mid-point review, exec readout.
transcript:
[00:00] Sam (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. We're aiming to scope the POC and get alignment on what success looks like. Quick intros?
[00:12] Elaine (Acme): Hi, Elaine Park here, head of MLOps. Marcus is with me, and Jordan from security.
[00:18] Marcus (Acme): Hey all.
[00:20] Priya (Redwood SE): Priya Patel, I'll own the technical side for Redwood.
[00:25] Jordan (Acme): Jordan Lee, security lead.
[00:28] Sam: Cool, high level: propose a 4-week POC. Kickoff + access week, 2 weeks of running benchmarks and integration, mid-point review at week 3, and executive readout week 4. Does that map to what you had in mind?
[00:42] Elaine: Yes that looks right. Our main success criteria are: parity with current latency for our user-facing completions, cost per 1,000 requests that meets our budget target, and no data exfil risk - so KMS + VPC is a must.
[00:56] Marcus: To add, we need to see throughput at our peak — we typically see 30 QPS sustained on our main endpoint and bursts to 120 QPS for short windows. Token mix is around 60 tokens in prompt, 120 tokens generation avg, but there are longer sessions too.
[01:15] Priya: Great, that's helpful. We'll build the benchmark plan around that distribution. For latency SLO, are you targeting p95 under 300ms or tighter?
[01:26] Elaine: Ideally p95 < 200ms for our critical flow, but we can accept up to 300ms for non-critical paths.
[01:33] Sam: Noted, p95 200ms target for the main flow. We'll include both hosted API and Redwood Dedicated run profiles in the benchmarks so you can compare economics and latency.
[01:46] Jordan: On security: we need SOC2 evidence, SAML/SSO integration, audit logs, and KMS support. For on-prem or private we might need an air-gapped option later.
[01:58] Priya: We have SOC2 docs and a security pack, we'll share the package. For POC we'll set up a Private deployment in your VPC (VPC peering or PrivateLink) or use Dedicated with VPC peering depending on comfort. We support KMS integration for key isolation.
[02:12] Marcus: What's the typical time to get the VPC peering + service account set up? We have strict change windows.
[02:17] Sam: In our experience, access setup takes 3-5 business days if the network team can approve the peering quickly and share the bastion credentials. We'll provide a clear access checklist.
[02:27] Elaine: Good, we'll try to prioritize that.
[02:30] Priya: For benchmarks, we'll run: 1) baseline latency/throughput with our sample traces, 2) workload replay with KV-cache warmup, 3) stress bursts to validate autoscaling behavior, and 4) cost-per-token analysis across model variants and quantization.
[02:46] Marcus: Can you explain KV-cache warmup? We've seen cache effects swing latency a lot.
[02:50] Priya: Sure, sorry sometimes transcription says KV cash or cash, but it's KV cache — we want to rehydrate the key-value cache to mimic real conversational sessions so the token generation path is realistic. We'll run warmup passes and measure cold vs warm starts.
[03:05] Jordan: Also need to ensure logs are retained for 90 days and we can pull out audit trails. Is that possible?
[03:11] Sam: Yes, we can push audit logs to your logging bucket or SIEM. We'll include retention config in the playbook.
[03:18] Elaine: What about data residency? Some of our PII must stay in the EU region for certain clients.
[03:23] Priya: We can pin region to EU for those flows in the POC. We'll note model routing and region pinning in the config.
[03:30] Sam: Let's talk success metrics concretely so we can pass/fail the POC: 1) p95 latency for main flow <= 200ms; 2) >=95% of requests succeed without model fallback; 3) cost per 1k requests within 1.5x of your budgeted cost for this flow; 4) security controls validated (SAML + KMS + audit logs).
[03:55] Marcus: That seems reasonable. On the cost target, can you give a rough expectation for hosted vs dedicated?
[04:02] Priya: We'll provide a cost model in the playbook. Roughly, Dedicated tends to give 20-40% unit cost improvement at steady state but requires reserved capacity; hosted has less setup. We'll include quantization options which may further reduce cost.
[04:16] Elaine: For the POC we'll want both comparisons so stakeholders can see TCO tradeoffs.
[04:20] Sam: OK. Timeline/milestones I propose:
[04:24] - Week 0 (kickoff): access checklist, share playbook, initial infra session
[04:29] - Week 1: access setup (VPC peering, SSO test user, KMS config), sample data and trace ingestion
[04:35] - Week 2: run baseline benchmarks & begin integration testing (replay traces, KV warmup)
[04:40] - Week 3: stress tests, autoscaling validation, mid-point review with demo of results
[04:45] - Week 4: final tuning, exec readout and decision (pass/fail + next steps)
[04:50] Elaine: Works for us. Mid-point review should show at least initial latency graphs and cost delta.
[04:55] Priya: We'll prepare a benchmark dashboard and a shared spreadsheet with raw metrics. I'll also capture sample request/response traces for debugging.
[05:05] Marcus: Please include tokenization stats and model version mapping. We sometimes see different model variants change tokenization behavior.
[05:12] Priya: Absolutely. We'll include model versioning and exact hashes, and quantization profile used.
[05:18] Jordan: For security review, we'll need to run a short threat modeling session. Can we schedule 30 minutes during week 1?
[05:24] Sam: Yes, we'll schedule a security deep dive with our security engineer.
[05:28] Elaine: Anything about legal/procurement? Our procurement may need a short SOW.
[05:32] Sam: We can draft a POC SOW and send it along with pricing lanes after kickoff. It will include scope, timeline and acceptance criteria.
[05:40] Marcus: For the dataset, can we use masked production traces? We can't expose PII.
[05:45] Priya: Totally — sanitized or synthetic data is fine. We can also work with a small mirrored subset.
[05:50] Elaine: Great. One more question: what tooling do you provide for cost monitoring during the POC?
[05:55] Sam: The Redwood Console will show per-route token counts, latency heatmaps, and cost breakdowns. We'll give you an account with RBAC so your finance and engineering stakeholders can view.
[06:06] Priya: And we'll export the raw metrics to the shared spreadsheet for your analysts.
[06:10] Marcus: Sounds good.
[06:12] Sam: Any final risks we should note?
[06:14] Jordan: Network change windows could delay access; procurement could delay the SOW.
[06:18] Elaine: Also need to validate KMS key import process end-to-end.
[06:22] Sam: We'll add contingency buffers — if access is delayed we'll shift the mid-point review but still aim to complete within 6 weeks.
[06:30] Priya: I'll follow up with a detailed benchmark plan and test harness steps.
[06:34] Sam: Recap of next steps: Sam sends POC playbook and SOW draft; Priya sends benchmark plan and spreadsheet template; Acme to provide logs and set up service account + SSO test user; schedule kickoff week of 2025-02-17.
[06:50] Elaine: Thanks everyone, we'll get the network folks looped in.
[06:55] Sam: Thanks all, we'll follow up in email with links to the playbook and the shared sheet.
[07:00] (call ends)
